'''Dorothy McCoy''' (August 9, 1903 – November 21, 2001) was an American [[mathematician]] and university professor. She was the first woman to earn a doctorate in mathematics from the [[University of Iowa]], and she worked for many years as a professor of mathematics at [[Belhaven University|Belhaven College]] and [[Wayland Baptist University|Wayland Baptist College]].

==Early life and education==
McCoy was born on August 9, 1903, in [[Waukomis, Oklahoma]], then part of the [[Oklahoma Territory]], one of two children of a homesteading family. She and the rest of the family moved to [[Chesapeake, Missouri]], in 1906 after the death of her father.<ref name=pioneer>{{cite book|last1=Green|first1=Judy|author1-link=Judy Green (mathematician)|last2=LaDuke|first2=Jeanne|author2-link=Jeanne LaDuke|contribution=McCoy, Dorothy, August 9, 1903 – November 21, 2001|date=January 2009|pages=240–241|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 PhD's|title-link=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics|contribution-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IRbOAwAAQBAJ&pg=PA240}} Reprinted in {{cite web|url=http://unger.myplainview.com/supplement.pdf|title=From Apples to WACS: A Supplement to the Second Edition of ''Hale County, Texas, Bibliography''|first=John|last=Sigwald|date=January 2016|pages=S52–S53|publisher=Unger Memorial Library|location=Plainview, Texas|access-date=2020-03-25}} See also more detailed biography on pp. 399–401 of [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary material for ''Pioneering Women in American Mathematics''].</ref> She received a bachelor's degree from [[Baylor University]] in Texas with distinction,<ref name=asc-awm>{{cite journal|url=https://pages.uoregon.edu/wmnmath/People/Biographies/McCoyInMemoriam.pdf|title=Dorothy McCoy (1903–2001)|department=In memoriam|journal=Association for Women in Mathematics Newsletter|volume=32|issue=1|date=January–February 2002}} Reprinted as {{Cite web|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/mccoy.htm|title=Dorothy McCoy|work=Biographies of Women Mathematicians|publisher=Agnes Scott College|first=Larry|last=Riddle|date=February 25, 2016|access-date=2020-03-25}}</ref> worked for a year as a mathematics teacher,<ref name=pioneer/> and completed a doctorate in mathematics from the [[University of Iowa]] in 1929,<ref name=asc-awm/> under the supervision of Edward Wilson Chittenden. Her dissertation was ''The Complete Existential Theory of Eight Fundamental Properties of Topological Spaces''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=43112}}</ref> She earned both degrees at the same time as her younger brother, [[Neal Henry McCoy|Neal]], who became a professor of mathematics at [[Smith College]].<ref name=asc-awm/> She became the first woman to earn a doctorate in mathematics at the University of Iowa, and (with [[Winifred Asprey]], Barbara Beechler, and Kathryn Powell Ellis) one of only four who did so before 1960.<ref>{{cite book|title=Women Becoming Mathematicians: Creating a Professional Identity in Post-World War II America|first=Margaret A. M.|last=Murray|publisher=MIT Press|year=2001|isbn=9780262632461|page=131|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Sz78C8-PGUQC&pg=PA131}}</ref>

==Later life and career==
McCoy became professor and head of the mathematics department at [[Belhaven University|Belhaven College]] in [[Mississippi]] in 1929, and 
chaired the Louisiana–Mississippi Section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 1937 and 1938.<ref name=pioneer/> In 1949 she became professor of mathematics and chair of the division of physical and biological sciences at [[Wayland Baptist University|Wayland Baptist College]]. She was a [[Fulbright Scholar]] in 1954, visiting Iraq, and later traveled professionally to many other countries. She also consulted for the US government's missile defense program. She retired as distinguished professor emerita in 1975, "the only member of the faculty to have received the title of both emeritus and distinguished".<ref name=asc-awm/>

She died on November 21, 2001.<ref name=obit>{{cite web|url=https://www.wbu.edu/news-and-events/archives/2001/december/mccoy-death.htm|title=Longtime Wayland supporter, former professor dies|publisher=Wayland Baptist University|date=November 29, 2001|access-date=2020-03-25}}</ref>

==Recognition==
The Wayland Baptist Association of Former Students gave McCoy their Distinguished Lifetime Service Award in 1999.<ref name=obit/> Wayland Baptist named a dorm in her honor in 2001,<ref name=obit/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wbu.edu/news-and-events/archives/2001/october/mccoy.htm|title=Wayland to dedicate honors dorm to former faculty member|publisher=Wayland Baptist University|date=October 5, 2001|access-date=2020-03-25}}</ref> and displays a bust of her in one of its buildings.<ref name=obit/>

Two photographs of her are included in the collection of the [[National Museum of American History]], as part of a set of photos on women with doctorates in mathematics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.edu/object/nmah_1300157|title=Photographs of Women with Doctorates in Mathematics|publisher=[[National Museum of American History]]|accessdate=2020-03-29}}</ref>
